abstract: [Radiology. Artificial intelligence] Purpose To develop and evaluate a deep learning model (DLLV) for identifying reduced left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) on chest radiographs (CXRs) and assess its potential as a prescreening tool for selective transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) in health checkup populations. Materials and Methods Same-day CXR-TTE pairs obtained between January 2016 and September 2021 were retrospectively collected for model development. Counterfactual learning was applied to enhance model performance and interpretability. External testing included one tertiary referral center cohort and two health checkup cohorts. Discrimination was evaluated using area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) and area under the precision-recall curve (AUPRC), and DLLV-based prescreening was evaluated by estimated TTE reduction and missed-case burden. Results The development dataset included 24,674 patients (32,135 CXR-TTE pairs); external cohorts included 5440, 28,034, and 6085 patients (53-62% male). DLLV achieved an AUC of 0.86 (95% CI: 0.84, 0.88) for LVEF ≤ 40% in the tertiary referral cohort. In health checkup cohorts, AUCs were 0.92-0.97 for LVEF ≤ 40%, with AUPRCs of 0.04 in both cohorts, corresponding to 87-fold (95% CI: 16, 404) and 37-fold (95% CI: 3, 251) enrichment over baseline prevalence. Counterfactual reinforcement learning produced heatmaps with greater heart localization precision (P < .001 for all) and higher AUC for LVEF < 50% (P = .04). DLLV-based prescreening estimated TTE volume reductions up to 85% while identifying all 12 and 7 individuals with LVEF ≤ 40%. Conclusion DLLV identified reduced LVEF on CXRs across external test cohorts and showed potential as a prescreening tool for selective TTE in health checkup populations. ©RSNA, 2026.
zh_abstract: 【目的】开发并评估一种用于在胸部X线摄影（CXRs）上识别左心室射血分数（LVEF）降低的深度学习模型（DLLV），并评估其在健康体检人群中作为选择性经胸超声心动图（TTE）预筛工具的潜力。【材料与方法】回顾性收集2016年1月至2021年9月期间获得的同日CXR-TTE配对数据用于模型开发。应用反事实学习以提高模型性能和可解释性。外部测试包括一个三级转诊中心队列和两个健康体检队列。使用受试者工作特征曲线下面积（AUC）和精确率-召回率曲线下面积（AUPRC）评估区分能力，并通过估计的TTE减少量和漏诊病例负担评估基于DLLV的预筛。【结果】开发数据集包括24,674例患者（32,135对CXR-TTE配对）；外部队列分别包括5440、28,034和6085例患者（男性占53–62%）。在三级转诊队列中，DLLV对LVEF ≤ 40%达到AUC为0.86（95% CI：0.84，0.88）。在健康体检队列中，对LVEF ≤ 40%的AUC为0.92–0.97，两个队列的AUPRC均为0.04，分别相当于较基线患病率富集87倍（95% CI：16，404）和37倍（95% CI：3，251）。反事实强化学习生成的热图具有更高的心脏定位精度（所有P < .001），并且对LVEF < 50%具有更高的AUC（P = .04）。基于DLLV的预筛估计可使TTE检查量减少最多85%，同时识别出全部12例和7例LVEF ≤ 40%的个体。【结论】DLLV在外部测试队列中识别出CXRs上的LVEF降低，并显示出作为健康体检人群中选择性TTE预筛工具的潜力。©RSNA, 2026。

abstract: [Radiology. Artificial intelligence] Purpose To develop and evaluate TRAM-AI, a consensus-based checklist for verifying whether medical imaging datasets described as publicly accessible are functionally usable for AI development. Materials and Methods A modified Delphi study was conducted. A steering committee generated candidate checklist items through a targeted literature review. An international expert panel (n = 33) rated items on criticality and feasibility across two Delphi rounds. Consensus was defined as ≥ 75% agreement on both dimensions. The checklist was pilot-validated in 10 publicly available datasets. An advisory group of four experts from Latin America and sub-Saharan Africa evaluated cross-regional applicability. Results Of 16 candidate items, 14 were retained in the final checklist; one item was removed because of feasibility concerns, and another was merged with an existing item because of conceptual redundancy. All 14 final items achieved consensus for both criticality and feasibility. The final TRAM-AI checklist comprises 14 items across four domains: Dataset Access and Persistence (3 items), Technical Interoperability (4 items), Metadata and Reproducibility (4 items), and Ethical, Legal, and Maintenance considerations (3 items). In pilot validation, all items were applicable to all 10 datasets, compliance was 90% for trusted repository, de-dentification, and subject-level mapping, 10% for archive validation, and 30% for partition keys. All four advisory group members endorsed the checklist. Conclusion TRAM-AI provides a practical framework for verifying the functional accessibility of medical imaging datasets, complementing existing methodological reporting standards. Further evaluation and broader validation across diverse geographic settings are warranted. ©RSNA, 2026.
zh_abstract: [Radiology. Artificial intelligence]【目的】开发并评估 TRAM-AI，一种基于共识的清单，用于核验被描述为可公开获取的医学影像数据集在功能上是否可用于人工智能（AI）开发。【材料与方法】开展了一项改良德尔菲研究。指导委员会通过定向文献综述生成候选清单条目。一个国际专家小组（n = 33）在两轮德尔菲中对条目的关键性和可行性进行评分。共识定义为两个维度均达到≥75%同意。该清单在10个公开可用数据集中进行了试点验证。由来自拉丁美洲和撒哈拉以南非洲的四名专家组成的顾问组评估了跨区域适用性。【结果】在16个候选条目中，14个被保留在最终清单中；1个条目因可行性担忧被删除，另1个条目因概念冗余与现有条目合并。所有14个最终条目在关键性和可行性两方面均达成共识。最终的 TRAM-AI 清单包含4个领域的14个条目：数据集获取与持久性（Dataset Access and Persistence，3个条目）、技术互操作性（Technical Interoperability，4个条目）、元数据与可重复性（Metadata and Reproducibility，4个条目），以及伦理、法律与维护考量（Ethical, Legal, and Maintenance considerations，3个条目）。在试点验证中，所有条目均适用于全部10个数据集；可信存储库、去标识化（de-dentification）和受试者层面映射的符合率为90%，归档验证为10%，分区键为30%。顾问组全部四名成员均认可该清单。【结论】TRAM-AI 提供了一个实用框架，用于核验医学影像数据集的功能可及性，补充现有方法学报告标准。有必要在不同地理环境中进一步评估和更广泛验证。©RSNA, 2026。

title: Artificial intelligence for symptom assessment and patient-reported outcomes in neuro-oncology.
zh_title: 人工智能用于神经肿瘤症状评估与患者报告结局
summary: 叙述性综述总结神经肿瘤患者报告结局的 AI 分析工具、真实世界应用考量与伦理问题。
key_points: 检索 2015–2026 年英文文献
纳入 53 篇文献进行主题综述
讨论 AI 分析 PRO 的应用与伦理
reason: 叙述性综述，非系统综述；信息有参考价值，属值得一看档
abstract: [Journal of neuro-oncology] Patient-reported outcomes (PROs) are critical tools for measuring how patients experience their illness and treatment. Neuropsychiatric symptoms, headaches, seizures, and neurological deficits evolve over time and impact quality of life. In this narrative review, we summarize current literature on PROs in neuro-oncology, extant artificial intelligence (AI) tools for PRO analysis, considerations for real-world application, and ethical implications. We searched PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, and Google Scholar for English-language articles published from January 2015 through April 2026, supplemented by reference-list reviews. Four themes were agreed upon, and authors were assigned to each theme. Authors conducted a literature review, selected articles, and synthesized the information under each of these themes. An initial 78 articles were narrowed down to 53 confirming eligibility if they reported PRO or symptom data in people with brain tumors or computational/AI methods were applied to PRO or symptom monitoring in oncology. Article selection was verified by two senior authors (L.V.Y, A.S.). Older, foundational studies were retained where they remain the primary evidence. The growing volume and complexity of PRO data present challenges for traditional analysis methods. Integrating AI, including machine learning (ML) and large language models (LLMs), may help model longitudinal symptom trajectories to predict deterioration, extract symptoms from free-text clinical notes, and embed outputs in clinical decision support tools. Autonomy, informed consent, data security, bias, access, transparency and accountability should be considered. Successful translation will require interpretable, electronic health record-integrated, bias-mitigating tools that allow for actionable insights and preserve patient consent, privacy, and autonomy in this highly vulnerable population. Not applicable.
zh_abstract: [Journal of Neuro-Oncology] 患者报告结局（patient-reported outcomes, PROs）是衡量患者如何体验其疾病和治疗的关键工具。神经精神症状、头痛、癫痫发作和神经功能缺损随时间演变并影响生活质量。在这篇叙述性综述中，我们总结了当前关于神经肿瘤学中PROs的文献、用于PRO分析的现有AI工具、真实世界应用的考虑以及伦理影响。我们检索了PubMed/MEDLINE、Embase和Google Scholar，纳入2015年1月至2026年4月发表的英文文章，并辅以参考文献列表审查。确定了四个主题，并为每个主题分配了作者。作者对每个主题进行了文献综述、筛选文章并综合信息。最初78篇文章缩小至53篇，若报告了脑肿瘤患者的PRO或症状数据，或计算/AI方法应用于肿瘤学中的PRO或症状监测，则确认符合纳入标准。文章选择由两位资深作者（L.V.Y, A.S.）核实。较早期的奠基性研究若仍是主要证据则予以保留。PRO数据数量和复杂性的不断增长给传统分析方法带来挑战。整合AI，包括机器学习（machine learning, ML）和大语言模型（large language models, LLMs），可能有助于建模纵向症状轨迹以预测恶化、从自由文本临床记录中提取症状，并将输出嵌入临床决策支持工具。应考虑自主性、知情同意、数据安全、偏倚、可及性、透明度和问责制。成功转化将需要可解释、整合电子健康记录、减轻偏倚的工具，这些工具能够提供可操作的见解，并在这一高度脆弱人群中维护患者同意、隐私和自主性。不适用。

title: MMedAgent-Plus: Scaling Multimodal Medical Agents across Modalities, Tasks and Workflows
zh_title: MMedAgent-Plus：跨模态跨任务的多模态医疗智能体
summary: 多模态医疗工具调用智能体，用视觉语言规划器调度18个专科模型，覆盖8种模态、12项任务。

reason: 预印本，方法清晰、训练规模大，但仅基准评测无外部临床验证，属值得一看档。
abstract: Medical workflows often require multiple interdependent analyses, but existing specialist and generalist AI models are not designed to coordinate them. We introduce MMedAgent-Plus, a multimodal medical tool-use agent that combines a vision-language planner with 18 leading specialist models spanning 12 tasks and 8 modalities. Through a unified tool interface, the planner selects specialists, executes them in sequence, and synthesizes responses grounded in their outputs. The planner is instruction-tuned on 208,928 samples from 32 public medical benchmarks, covering single- and multi-tool interactions across single and multiple rounds. We separately evaluate tool orchestration, response synthesis, and end-to-end execution on held-out samples. MMedAgent-Plus achieves tool-call accuracies of 91.0%, 98.1%, and 80.7% in single-tool multi-round, multi-tool multi-round, and multi-tool single-round settings, respectively. Given correct tool outputs, MMedAgent-Plus achieves scores of 14.4-14.8 out of 15 for faithfulness, completeness, and conciseness across 600 evaluation samples. In end-to-end execution without pre-supplied tool outputs, MMedAgent-Plus correctly invokes the required specialist in 90.6% of 350 evaluation cases spanning seven tasks. Its final-answer accuracy reaches 0.98, matching the dedicated leading specialist and exceeding the strongest baseline (0.28).
zh_abstract: 医学工作流程常需要多项相互依赖的分析，但现有的专科与通用 AI 模型并非为协调这些分析而设计。我们提出 MMedAgent-Plus，一种多模态医学工具使用智能体，它将视觉-语言规划器与 18 个领先的专科模型相结合，涵盖 12 项任务和 8 种模态。通过统一工具接口，规划器选择专科模型，按顺序执行它们，并综合基于其输出的回答。规划器在来自 32 个公共医学基准的 208,928 个样本上进行指令微调，覆盖单轮和多轮中的单工具与多工具交互。我们分别在留出样本上评估工具编排、回答综合和端到端执行。MMedAgent-Plus 在单工具多轮、多工具多轮和多工具单轮设置中分别达到 91.0%、98.1% 和 80.7% 的工具调用准确率。在给定正确工具输出的情况下，MMedAgent-Plus 在 600 个评估样本上的忠实性、完整性和简洁性得分达到 15 分中的 14.4-14.8 分。在未预先提供工具输出的端到端执行中，MMedAgent-Plus 在涵盖七项任务的 350 个评估案例中，有 90.6% 正确调用了所需的专科模型。其最终答案准确率达到 0.98，与专门的领先专科模型相当，并超过最强基线（0.28）。

title: AI chatbots abandon sleep apnoea referral when simulated patients minimise symptoms
zh_title: 患者淡化症状时AI聊天机器人放弃睡眠呼吸暂停转诊
summary: 在700段模拟对话中检验五款免费聊天机器人于患者淡化症状时是否仍维持指南一致的OSA转诊。
abstract: BackgroundPatients increasingly consult free artificial intelligence (AI) chatbots about their symptoms, but these models may favour agreement with the patient over accuracy. In obstructive sleep apnoea (OSA), where most cases in the general population remain undiagnosed and diagnosis depends on referral, this could validate symptom denial. We tested whether consumer chatbots maintain guideline-concordant referral when a simulated patient minimises symptoms. MethodsSeven guideline-concordant and standardised OSA vignettes (apnoea-hypopnoea-index, AHI 8-52 events/h; body mass index 28-42 kg/m2) were presented to five free chatbots (GPT-5, Gemini 2.5 Flash, Claude Sonnet 4.6, DeepSeek V4 Flash and Grok-4.3) under neutral and symptom-minimising conditions (10 simulated conversations per model- vignette-condition cell; N=700). Referral maintenance was scored by a structured rubric and every capitulation was human-confirmed. ResultsAll chatbots maintained referral recommendations in neutral conversations (350/350; 100%). When simulated patients minimised symptoms and resisted referral, maintenance fell to 64.3% (225/350), a reduction of 35.7 percentage points (95% CI 5.5- 66.0; p=0.028). Rates ranged from 55.7% to 85.7% across chatbots, but evidence of between-chatbot differences was inconsistent across analyses. Rates differed across clinical vignettes (p=0.001). A variance analysis estimated greater variation between vignettes than between chatbots. In the three driving-risk vignettes, referral recommendations were abandoned in 46- 68% of symptom-minimising conversations, pooling all five chatbots within each vignette. ConclusionsConsumer AI chatbots abandoned correct OSA referral recommendations in about one-third of symptom-minimising conversations, with higher observed abandonment in simulated cases involving driving risk. This may delay appropriate assessment and raises patient- and public-safety concerns.

abstract: Cancer care is a longitudinal, time-sensitive process requiring coordination among diverse healthcare professionals (HCPs), whose collaboration evolves throughout treatment. Prior studies link care team structure to patient outcomes, but the temporal dynamics of collaboration and their relationship to evolving patient risk remain poorly understood. We introduce a visual analytics framework for modeling and interpreting time-varying care team interactions in oncology. We construct dynamic collaboration networks from electronic health record (EHR)-mediated communication data and use a temporal graph neural network (TGNN) to estimate patient outcome risk over time. We then investigate how changes in care team composition and specialist participation relate to shifts in estimated risk across treatment stages. Our multi-view interactive system combines TGNN-based risk modeling with coordinated visualizations of care team networks, feature-level explanations from a surrogate logistic regression model, and exploratory what-if analysis. Without making causal claims, the system helps analysts examine how risk estimates co-evolve with collaboration patterns and identify care team characteristics associated with these changes. We demonstrate its utility through expert-guided analysis scenarios involving 505 patients with breast, colorectal, and lung cancers, evaluating its ability to reveal clinically meaningful collaboration patterns. This work improves the interpretability of temporal graph-based models in longitudinal, team-based healthcare, with potential applicability to other evolving collaborative settings.
zh_abstract: 癌症照护是一个纵向、时间敏感的过程，需要不同医疗保健专业人员（healthcare professionals, HCPs）之间的协调，他们的协作在整个治疗过程中不断演变。既往研究将照护团队结构与患者结局联系起来，但协作的时间动态及其与不断变化的患者风险之间的关系仍知之甚少。我们引入一个可视分析框架，用于建模和解释肿瘤学中随时间变化的照护团队互动。我们从电子健康记录（electronic health record, EHR）介导的沟通数据构建动态协作网络，并使用时间图神经网络（temporal graph neural network, TGNN）来估计患者随时间变化的结局风险。然后我们研究照护团队构成和专科医生参与的变化如何与不同治疗阶段估计风险的转变相关。我们的多视图交互系统将基于TGNN的风险建模与照护团队网络的协调可视化、来自代理逻辑回归模型的特征层面解释以及探索性假设情景分析相结合。该系统不作因果断言，帮助分析人员检查风险估计如何与协作模式共同演变，并识别与这些变化相关的照护团队特征。我们通过涉及505名乳腺癌、结直肠癌和肺癌患者的专家引导分析场景展示其效用，评估其揭示具有临床意义的协作模式的能力。这项工作提高了时间图模型在纵向、团队式医疗保健中的可解释性，并可能适用于其他不断演变的协作环境。

title: Cross-database adaptation of machine learning models for predicting sustained antibiotic exposure among patients with intracerebral hemorrhage in intensive care units

abstract: BackgroundPatients with intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) in intensive care units (ICUs) frequently receive antibiotics early in critical illness. Such exposure reflects suspected infection, physiological deterioration, monitoring intensity, and clinical management and may vary across institutions and electronic health record databases. We evaluated target-domain adaptation for modeling sustained antibiotic exposure in critically ill patients with ICH. MethodsWe analyzed derived ICH cohorts from MIMIC-IV and the eICU Collaborative Research Database. MIMIC-IV included 2,024 ICU stays and served as the source cohort. The eICU cohort comprised 1,277 stays and was divided, at the ICU-stay level, into a development subset (766 stays) and a held-out evaluation subset (511 stays). The eICU outcome was sustained antibiotic exposure on at least two ICU days. Candidate models incorporated demographic, comorbidity, physiological, laboratory, neurologic, respiratory, temporal, and measurementprocess features. Timestamped observations for static and temporal tabular families were censored at the recorded first-antibiotic time when available, whereas the compact sequence component and explicit measurement-density features used the full first 24 hours. For base-model families using eICU development data, meta-learner inputs were generated by five-fold stratified cross-fitting. A 42-input L2-penalized logistic meta-learner combined 16 model probabilities with model-summary, clinical, availability, and measurement-density features. ResultsThe held-out eICU subset contained 48 positive outcomes (9.39%). The adapted ensemble achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) of 0.841 (95% CI 0.775-0.899) and an average precision (AP) of 0.540 (95% CI 0.399-0.676), with a Brier score of 0.063 and expected calibration error of 0.029. The MIMIC-IV source-only stack achieved an AUROC of 0.782; the paired AUROC difference was 0.059 (95% CI 0.003-0.112). In a separate patient-grouped five-fold out-of-fold sensitivity analysis of 503 linked eICU stays, AUROC was 0.807 (95% CI 0.691-0.910). ConclusionsTarget-domain adaptation improved held-out discrimination relative to a source-only stack for sustained antibiotic exposure. title: Advances in Multimodal Artificial Intelligence in Radiology: Data Integration, Foundation Models, and Clinical Applications-A Narrative Review.
zh_title: 放射学多模态AI进展：数据整合、基础模型与临床应用
summary: 叙述性综述，检索9个数据库从1154条记录中筛出111篇文献，梳理放射学多模态AI的技术与临床进展及落地障碍。
abstract: [Healthcare (Basel, Switzerland)] Background/Objectives: Multimodal artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly used in radiology to combine medical images with radiology reports, clinical narratives, structured health records, laboratory measurements, and other patient data. These systems may support more context-aware interpretation, reporting, and clinical decision-making than unimodal approaches. This narrative review examines recent technical and clinical advances in multimodal radiology AI and identifies barriers to responsible implementation. Methods: Relevant biomedical and technical literature was identified through targeted searches of PubMed, IEEE Xplore, ACM Digital Library, Web of Science, Scopus, arXiv, ScienceDirect, SpringerLink, and Google Scholar. A documented screening process identified 111 reviewed publications from 1154 records. Study selection and data extraction were conducted by one reviewer without independent verification. Original research, reviews, and commentaries, including selected preprints, were synthesized thematically. Results: The field has progressed from early and late feature fusion toward cross-modal attention, contrastive image-text pretraining, vision-language models, multimodal large language models, and general-purpose foundation models. Applications include diagnostic classification, prognostic modelling, image-text retrieval, visual question answering, clinical decision support, and automated radiology report generation. Despite promising technical results, comparison across studies remains difficult because of heterogeneous datasets, tasks, metrics, and validation designs. Clinical translation is further limited by scarce external and prospective validation, uncertain interpretability, hallucination and omission risks, privacy and fairness concerns, and limited real-world workflow evaluation. Conclusions: Multimodal AI may enable more clinically informed radiological interpretation and reporting, but progress in benchmark performance has outpaced evidence of safety, generalizability, and clinical utility. Future research should prioritize multicentre evaluation, clinically meaningful metrics, transparent reporting, robust safety assessment, and workflow-centred implementation.

zh_abstract: [Healthcare (Basel, Switzerland)]【背景/目的】多模态人工智能（AI）越来越多地用于放射学，将医学图像与放射学报告、临床叙述、结构化健康记录、实验室检测及其他患者数据相结合。与单模态方法相比，这些系统可能支持更具情境感知能力的解读、报告和临床决策。本叙述性综述考察多模态放射学 AI 的近期技术与临床进展，并识别负责任实施的障碍。【方法】通过定向检索 PubMed、IEEE Xplore、ACM Digital Library、Web of Science、Scopus、arXiv、ScienceDirect、SpringerLink 和 Google Scholar，识别相关生物医学和技术文献。有记录的筛选流程从1154条记录中确定了111篇纳入综述的出版物。研究选择和数据提取由一名评审员完成，未经独立核验。原始研究、综述和评论（包括部分预印本）按主题进行综合。【结果】该领域已从早期和晚期特征融合发展到跨模态注意力、对比图像-文本预训练、视觉-语言模型、多模态大语言模型和通用基础模型。应用包括诊断分类、预后建模、图像-文本检索、视觉问答、临床决策支持和自动化放射学报告生成。尽管技术结果前景良好，但由于数据集、任务、指标和验证设计异质，研究间比较仍然困难。临床转化进一步受到以下因素限制：外部验证和前瞻性验证稀缺、可解释性不确定、幻觉和遗漏风险、隐私和公平性担忧，以及真实世界工作流程评估有限。【结论】多模态 AI 可能促成更具临床信息支持的放射学解读和报告，但基准性能的进展已超过安全性、泛化性和临床效用方面的证据。未来研究应优先开展多中心评估、采用具有临床意义的指标、透明报告、稳健的安全性评估和以工作流程为中心的实施。

title: AI-Assisted Patient Education Before Suturing in Minor Trauma
zh_title: AI辅助缝合前患者教育试验
summary: Gazi大学注册的干预性试验，拟入组96例急诊小创伤缝合患者，评估AI辅助术前患者教育对疼痛与焦虑的影响。
abstract: [Newly registered clinical trial, no results yet; sponsor: Gazi University; conditions: Minor Trauma Requiring Suturing, Pain, Anxiety; type: INTERVENTIONAL; phase: NA; enrollment: 96; status: RECRUITING] Patients scheduled to undergo suturing for minor trauma in the emergency department frequently experience anticipatory pain and anxiety before the procedure. These experiences may negatively affect perceived pain, cooperation with treatment, adherence, satisfaction, and the overall care experience. However, the realities of emergency department practice, including crowding, high patient volume, staff shortages, and increased workload, may limit effective nurse-patient communication and comprehensive patient education. Patients awaiting suturing for minor trauma often experience uncertainty, prolonged waiting, fear of the procedure, and concern about pain. These factors may increase anxiety, which can further intensify pain perception and negatively influence patients' cooperation with treatment and satisfaction with care. Previous reports indicate that many patients waiting in emergency departments seek information about waiting times, care processes, and their medical conditions, highlighting a substantial need for accessible and reliable information. During this waiting period, patients may increasingly use artificial intelligence-based digital resources to obtain information about their health condition and the procedure they are about to undergo. However, information generated by artificial intelligence may be inaccurate, incomplete, or insufficiently tailored to the clinical context. Therefore, such information should be reviewed and validated by healthcare professionals before being provided to patients. This study aims to evaluate the effect of an artificial intelligence-assisted patient education material delivered during the pre-suturing waiting period on pain and anxiety levels among patients with minor trauma in the emergency department. It is also expected that the educational material developed within the scope of this study may contribute to patient education and supportive care in emergency department settings.

zh_abstract: [新注册临床试验，尚无结果；申办方：加齐大学（Gazi University）；疾病/状况：需要缝合的轻微创伤、疼痛、焦虑；类型：干预性；分期：NA；入组人数：96；状态：招募中]计划在急诊科接受轻微创伤缝合的患者，常在操作前经历预期性疼痛和焦虑。这些体验可能对感知疼痛、治疗配合度、依从性、满意度及整体照护体验产生负面影响。然而，急诊科实践的现实情况，包括拥挤、患者量大、人员短缺和工作量增加，可能限制有效的护患沟通和全面的患者教育。等待轻微创伤缝合的患者常经历不确定性、等待时间延长、对操作的恐惧和对疼痛的担忧。这些因素可能增加焦虑，而焦虑又可进一步加重疼痛感知，并对患者治疗配合度和照护满意度产生负面影响。既往报告表明，许多在急诊科等待的患者会寻求关于等待时间、照护流程及其医疗状况的信息，凸显了对可获取且可靠信息的巨大需求。在此等待期间，患者可能越来越多地使用基于人工智能的数字资源来获取有关其健康状况和即将接受操作的信息。然而，人工智能生成的信息可能不准确、不完整，或未充分贴合临床情境。因此，此类信息在提供给患者之前应由医疗专业人员审核和验证。本研究旨在评估在缝合前等待期间提供的人工智能辅助患者教育材料对急诊科轻微创伤患者疼痛和焦虑水平的影响。还预期本研究范围内开发的教育材料可能有助于急诊科环境中的患者教育和支持性照护。

title: The Impact of Artificial Intelligence-Assisted X-ray Interpretation on Radiologists' Diagnostic Performance
zh_title: AI 辅助 X 线阅片对放射科医生诊断表现的影响
summary: 一项新注册观察性研究拟比较放射科医生在有无 AI 辅助时阅读 X 线的诊断表现。
abstract: [Newly registered clinical trial, no results yet; sponsor: The Third Affiliated Hospital of Southern Medical University; conditions: Pneumothorax, Intestinal Obstruction, Spondylolysis, Renal Calculus; type: OBSERVATIONAL; enrollment: 500; status: NOT_YET_RECRUITING] This study tests whether an artificial intelligence (AI) tool helps radiologists read X-rays more accurately. Radiologists read X-rays to find diseases such as pneumonia, bone fractures, and abdominal problems. AI is a computer program trained on many past X-rays. It may help radiologists spot diseases faster and more correctly. This study compares reading X-rays with the AI tool to reading X-rays without it. Who takes part * Ten radiologists from several hospitals. * X-ray images from about 300 to 500 past hospital visits. * No new X-rays are taken. * All names and ID numbers are removed from the images. What happens * Each radiologist reads the same set of X-rays twice. * One time, the radiologist reads without the AI tool. * The other time, the radiologist can see the AI result. * Half start with no AI and then switch to AI. The other half start with AI and then switch to no AI. * There is a four-week break between the two times. * The researchers measure how accurate each radiologist is. They also time how long each image takes. Possible benefits and risks * The radiologists may get no direct personal benefit. * The results may show whether AI can help doctors read X-rays better in the future. * This is a low-risk study. The AI tool never tells a patient a diagnosis directly. * A qualified radiologist always makes the final diagnosis. * Patient data is stored on a locked, encrypted server.

zh_abstract: [新注册临床试验，尚无结果；申办者：南方医科大学第三附属医院；疾病：气胸、肠梗阻、椎弓峡部裂、肾结石；类型：观察性；入组人数：500；状态：尚未招募] 本研究检验一种人工智能（artificial intelligence, AI）工具是否能帮助放射科医生更准确地阅读X射线。放射科医生阅读X射线以发现肺炎、骨折和腹部问题等疾病。AI是一种用许多既往X射线训练过的计算机程序。它可能帮助放射科医生更快、更正确地发现疾病。本研究比较使用AI工具阅读X射线与不使用AI工具阅读X射线。谁参与 * 来自数家医院的十名放射科医生。* 来自大约300至500次既往医院就诊的X射线图像。* 不拍摄新的X射线。* 所有姓名和ID号码均从图像中移除。会发生什么 * 每位放射科医生两次阅读同一组X射线。* 一次，放射科医生不使用AI工具阅读。* 另一次，放射科医生可以看到AI结果。* 一半先不使用AI，然后切换到AI。另一半先使用AI，然后切换到不使用AI。* 两次之间有四周的间隔。* 研究人员测量每位放射科医生的准确度。他们还记录每张图像所需时间。可能的获益和风险 * 放射科医生可能不会获得直接的个人获益。* 结果可能显示AI未来是否能帮助医生更好地阅读X射线。* 这是一项低风险研究。AI工具从不直接告诉患者诊断。* 合格的放射科医生始终做出最终诊断。* 患者数据存储在锁定、加密的服务器上。
